cues.text: A school garden needs a fence. Would counting the squares inside tell us how much fencing to buy? Imagine walking all the way around its edge. That journey measures the boundary, which is called the perimeter.
cues.asr_text: A SCHOOL GARDEN NEEDS A FENCE WOULD COUNTING THE SQUARES INSIDE TELL US HOW MUCH FENCE TO BUY IMAGINE WALKING ALL THE WAY AROUND ITS EDGE THAT JOURNEY MEASURES THE BOUNDARY WHICH IS CALLED THE PERIMETER

cues.text: Our learning goal is to find the perimeter of regular and irregular shapes.
board: Find the perimeter of regular and irregular shapes.
cues.asr_text: OUR LEARNING GOAL IS TO FIND THE PERIMETER OF REGULAR AND IRREGULAR SHAPES

board_events.text: Find the perimeter of regular and irregular shapes.

cues.text: Success criteria. I can trace the complete outside boundary. I can use matching length units. I can find missing lengths before adding sides.
board: 3. Find missing lengths before adding sides.
cues.asr_text: SUCCESS CRITERIA I CAN TRACE THE COMPLETE OUTSIDE BOUNDARY I CAN USE MATCHING LENGTH UNITS I CAN FIND MISSING LENGTHS BEFORE ADDING SIDES

board_events.text: 3. Find missing lengths before adding sides.

cues.text: Use string to trace a shape, then straighten the string beside a ruler. This makes the idea of perimeter concrete. On a diagram, follow every outside side once and add those lengths using matching units. An inside dividing line is not part of the outside boundary.
cues.asr_text: USE STRING TO TRACE A SHAPE THEN STRAIGHTEN THE STRING BESIDE A RULER THIS MAKES THE IDEA OF PERIMETER CONCRETE ON A DIAGRAM FOLLOW EVERY OUTSIDE ONCE AND ADD THOSE LINKS USING MATCHING UNITS AN INSIDE DIVIDING LINE IS NOT PART OF THE OUTSIDE BOUNDARY

cues.text: A rectangular garden is seven metres long and four metres wide. Opposite sides have matching lengths. Trace the four edges and predict the total before we add them.
cues.asr_text: A RECTANGULAR GARDEN IS SEVEN METERS LONG AND FOUR METRES WIDE OPPOSITE SIDES HAVE MATCHING LENGTHS TRACE THE FOUR EDGES AND PREDICT THE TOTAL BEFORE WE ADD THEM

cues.text: Seven plus four plus seven plus four is twenty-two metres. We can also add seven and four, then double eleven. Both methods count the complete boundary exactly once.
cues.asr_text: SEVEN PLUS FOUR PLUS SEVEN PLUS FOUR IS TWENTY TWO METRES WE CAN ALSO ADD SEVEN AND FOUR THEN DOUBLE ELEVEN BOTH METHODS COUNT THE COMPLETE BOUNDARY EXACTLY ONCE

cues.text: Now trace an L-shaped garden. Its top is eight metres and its left side is six. A three-by-two rectangle is missing from the lower right corner. Use subtraction to find the remaining straight lengths.
cues.asr_text: NOW TRACE AN L SHAPED GARDEN ITS TOP IS EIGHT METERS AND ITS LEFT SIDE IS SIX AT THREE BY TWO RECTANGLE IS MISSING FROM THE LOWER RIGHT CORNER USE SUBTRACTION TO FIND THE REMAINING STRAIGHT LENGTHS

cues.text: The six outside edges measure eight, four, three, two, five and six metres. Their sum is twenty-eight metres. The inward corner still belongs to the outside boundary, so include both of its edges.
cues.asr_text: THE SIX OUTSIDE EDGES MEASURE EIGHT FORTY THREE TWO FIVE AND SIX METRES THEIR SUM IS TWENTY EIGHT METRES THE INWARD CORNER STILL BELONGS TO THE OUTSIDE BOUNDARY SO INCLUDE BOTH OF ITS EDGES

cues.text: Seven times four counts square units covering this rectangle. It does not measure the fence. For perimeter, trace and add the outside lengths. A useful check is whether your answer has metres or square metres.
cues.chapter: Do not multiply for a boundary length
cues.asr_text: SEVEN TIMES FOUR COUNTS SQUARE UNITS COVERING THIS RECTANGLE IT DOES NOT MEASURE THE FENCE FOR PERIMETER TRACE AND ADD THE OUTSIDE LENGTHS A USEFUL CHECK IS WHETHER YOUR ANSWER HAS METRES OR SQUARE METERS

cues.text: A rectangle is six metres by three metres. What is its perimeter? Look at the model, and keep your prediction in mind.
cues.asr_text: A RECTANGLE IS SIX METERS BY THREE METERS WHAT IS ITS PERIMETER LOOK AT THE MODEL AND KEEP YOUR PREDICTION IN MIND

cues.text: Six plus three makes nine. Double nine for the four sides: eighteen metres. Check by tracing and adding six, three, six and three.
cues.asr_text: SIX PLUS THREE MAKES NINE DOUBLE NINE FOR THE FOUR SIDES EIGHTEEN METRES CHECK BY TRACING AND ADDING SIX THREE SIX AND THREE

cues.text: Perimeter is a length around the complete outside edge. Trace before calculating, find hidden lengths and keep units consistent. Try outlining a book with string, then compare a direct measurement with the total of its side lengths. Reflect on which model helped you and why. Now try the MathMagic practice, and explain your thinking to someone.
